_comment: Whole network, one tile -- the measured optimum. Sweeping k=1,2,3,4,5 at the residual-block boundaries (qnn_models/slicing_study/experiments.jsonl, labels dronet_k*) shows every extra tile costs 0.367-0.379 ms of DSP dispatch against a 0.659 ms whole-network graph, so the k=1 critical path (0.659 ms on dsp) is never beaten: k=2 1.030, k=3 1.243, k=4 1.228, k=5 1.308 ms. Every dronet tile composes on HTA at every granularity tried, so the cut is a free choice -- it just does not pay. dronet_k2_head in the journal is the one alternative worth knowing: backbone ops 0-26 on HTA (1.394 ms) plus the two head convs on CPU int8 (0.012 ms) is 1.406 ms, cheaper than any whole-network placement that is not the DSP.

_provenance.statistic: median of per-sweep median_us, performance governor, CPU cells unmasked
